> 南郭子綦隱機而坐，仰天而噓，荅焉似喪其耦。

A man sits, leans back, breathes out, and looks as though he has lost his counterpart. His student asks whether a body can be made like dry wood and a mind like dead ash.

The chapter that follows is usually summarized as "all things are equal." That summary is wrong in a specific way, and the character 齊 is where it goes wrong.

## 齊 is grain, leveled

齊, bronze script: ears of grain brought to a uniform height. The original sense is leveled, even, uniform.

So the common reading seems right: 齊物 = all things are equal. But the book distinguishes two kinds of leveling:

- 俗解之齊: merging, unifying, forcing difference into one mold. That is 合 — the manufactured join.
- 莊子之齊: 齊於道. Every judgment, every division, is held inside the pivot, and no one end suppresses the other. That is 和.

齊物論 is not "there are no differences." It is: differences exist, each thing has its own face, and inside the way they no longer form oppositions. Difference without antagonism.

## 籟: the wind has no conductor

籟 is a bamboo flute, extended to any sound made through an aperture.

人籟 is music a person plays. 地籟 is the sound of ten thousand hollows when the wind passes. 天籟 is the hard one: there is no master producing it. Each aperture takes its own sound, rises and stops on its own.

This is the chapter's argument in miniature. The usual assumption is that behind many voices there must be one voice that authorizes them — a ruler, a sage, a standard. 天籟 says the many are self-authorizing, and nothing is missing when no one conducts.

## 樞 is a door pivot

樞 is the pivot of a door: at the center of the ring, leaning toward no side, turning to meet all four directions.

道樞, 環中: the pivot inside the ring. Standing there does not mean standing above the argument. It means the argument no longer has a side to stand on.

## 封: the line was drawn by a sentence

封, bronze script: a hand heaping earth, marking a boundary.

道 has no 封. Boundaries are drawn by speech — by 是非, by the sentence "this is so, that is not." Every boundary is a sentence that succeeded in being believed.

## 物化 is not reincarnation

The chapter ends with 莊周 dreaming he is a butterfly, waking, and not knowing which he is. 化 here is the same 化 as in chapter one: two people inverted, transforming.

物化 is not one thing turning into another. It is the boundary dissolving — forms flowing into one another, with no ledger kept of which was real.

## The test

Take one judgment you hold as universal — not a preference, a judgment about how things are. Then find the sentence that drew its boundary. 齊 does not require you to abandon the judgment. It requires you to know it is drawn.
